heroHeadline: Hemedti Formally Stripped of TSC Role — Malik Agar Appointed Deputy; SAF Seizes Wadi al-Atrun as Nyala Aerial Campaign Enters Day 5
heroSubtitle: On Day 1130, al-Burhan signed a constitutional decree formally removing Hemedti from the Transitional Sovereignty Council and appointing SPLM-N leader Malik Agar as TSC deputy — the final legal step stripping RSF of any state standing following the May 18 derecognition order and payroll cutoff. Simultaneously, SAF forces captured Wadi al-Atrun in Al-Malha locality, North Darfur, severing an RSF trans-Saharan supply corridor from Libya into Darfur used by RSF and Haftar LNA networks. SAF drone strikes on Nyala extended to a fifth consecutive day; the RSF cut all telecommunications in the city to suppress documentation of damage and casualties. Hemedti — reportedly still in Nyala — now faces simultaneous military pressure, a payroll crisis stripping RSF fighters of state salaries, and complete political delegitimization under Sudanese law. The RSF's ability to sustain operations from Nyala and Darfur increasingly depends on non-state supply chains as SAF closes northern (Wadi al-Atrun), eastern (Gedaref), and aerial corridors. Humanitarian conditions remain catastrophic: 19.5 million Sudanese face acute food insecurity with a lean-season peak of 28.9 million projected for June–August 2026.
